ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all partners, authorized representatives, and beneficial owners against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, Hong Kong Monetary Authority AML/CFT guidance and prohibitory notices, and PRC domestic terrorist and sanction lists. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, adverse media checks, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Screening must be completed pre-formation, prior to bank account opening, and before any high-risk cross-border transfer; results must be documented and retained for at least five years under Cap. 615. Any positive match requires immediate filing with the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit and refusal to proceed until clearance is obtained.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry e-Services Name Search and Integrated Companies Registry Information System; for Mainland FIP registration, SAMR State Administration for Market Regulation Enterprise Name Registration and Management System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: For the Hong Kong entity and the Mainland Foreign-Invested Partnership, names must comply with the respective statutory language rules. Hong Kong permits English and/or Traditional Chinese names; Mainland FIP names require Simplified Chinese characters and may include a corresponding English name. The four-tier naming convention consists of (1) administrative division or jurisdiction prefix, (2) distinctive trade name, (3) industry or business activity descriptor, and (4) legal form suffix, such as 'Foreign-Invested Partnership' or 'Limited Partnership'. Phonetic transliteration is required where the investor name is in Latin script, using standard Mandarin pinyin; the transliteration must be consistent across all corporate documents, bank records, and government filings. A direct translation may be used when phonetic transliteration is impractical, but it must be faithful and approved by the registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects a proposed name, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal within 14 days of receiving the rejection notice. The appeal must be submitted through the same online portal (SAMR or Companies Registry e-services) and must include a copy of the rejection notice, a legal memo explaining why the name is not prohibited or confusingly similar to an existing trade name, and a proposed revised name if the original is incurably defective. The registry must issue a written decision within 15 working days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may escalate within 30 days to the provincial or municipal SAMR administrative reconsideration body in the Mainland, or to the Companies Tribunal in Hong Kong, followed by judicial review before the appropriate court. The applicant may simultaneously reserve a revised name to avoid expiry of the statutory deadline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the sole registered address for a Hong Kong entity or a Mainland Foreign-Invested Partnership engaged in tabletop dice casting. The Hong Kong Companies Registry requires a physical registered office address accessible to regulators and process servers, and the Inland Revenue Department will reject a virtual mailbox for business registration. For the Mainland FIP, SAMR and local tax authorities require a physical business premises within the registered administrative district, supported by a lease contract and on-site evidence commensurate with the industry. A virtual address may be used only as a supplementary correspondence address, never as the exclusive registered address. The production facility for epoxy resin dice casting must be a physical location with proper commercial zoning, fire safety compliance, environmental permits, and employee presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) verify exact address matches lease and business license; (2) confirm premises exist and are accessible during business hours; (3) ensure visible signage matching the registered name; (4) maintain on-site equipment and inventory consistent with dice casting; (5) store production materials, molds, epoxy resins, finished goods, and shipping records on-site; (6) keep corporate records, VAT invoices, payroll records, and statutory registers at the location; (7) retain rent payment receipts, utility bills, and property tax records in the entity's name; (8) verify zoning permits light manufacturing and no residential restriction. Quantified risk: for a Hong Kong-registered manufacturer with a Mainland FIP base, the combined risk of an unannounced inspection by municipal tax authorities, SAMR, or customs is estimated at 15-25% per year; the risk rises to 40-50% within the first 12 months after VAT registration or customs registration; use of a pure virtual mailbox raises inspection risk to approximately 75-100% upon any regulator query or bank address discrepancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; official electronic portal: the China Electronic Tax Administration (e-Tax) system. Hong Kong SAR maintains a separate taxation regime under the Inland Revenue Department, but the national tax identity for this China-domiciled Foreign-Invested Partnership is registered with the STA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) formed in mainland China, the partnership must complete tax registration with the competent local STA office within 30 calendar days after the Administration for Market Regulation issues the business licence. Tax registration is integrated with business registration, so the partnership automatically receives the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code, which functions as its national Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and VAT ID. A foreign non-resident partner that needs a separate non-resident TIN must file a written registration application through the e-Tax portal using the official non-resident enterprise registration procedure, accompanied by the partnership agreement, the FIP registration certificate, the foreign partner's Hong Kong incorporation/business registration certificate (where applicable), certified identity documents of the partners, and a power of attorney appointing a resident tax representative. The STA verifies the dossier, issues the non-resident TIN, activates the partnership's e-Tax account, and grants access to electronic VAT invoice issuance and general-taxpayer status where eligible.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for income-tax entity classification: the PRC does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections, and the partnership's pass-through status is statutory. The only available elections are the VAT general-taxpayer election for registrants with annual taxable sales below RMB 5,000,000, and the simplified VAT levy method election for small-scale taxpayers.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis turnover threshold for VAT registration: any entity engaging in taxable sales of goods in China must register for VAT from its first taxable transaction. Compulsory VAT general-taxpayer registration applies once annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000; below that amount, the taxpayer may remain a small-scale taxpayer subject to simplified VAT rates.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory use of the National Unified Electronic Invoice Platform (the Fully Digitalised Electronic Invoice system) for all VAT-invoicing partnerships. Invoice XML data must be transmitted in real time to the STA through the official e-invoice API. The platform assigns a unique invoice number and QR code, performs automated anti-fraud validation and digital authentication, and retains the invoice in the national invoice database; legacy tax-control physical invoice devices are permitted only on a transitional basis for paper-invoice users.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The FIP may claim 0% VAT on export sales of the cast epoxy-resin polyhedral dice if it is a registered VAT general taxpayer, the goods are physically exported from the PRC customs territory under a direct export customs declaration made in the partnership's name, title and risk pass to the overseas customer, the goods are not prohibited from export, the export sales invoice is issued, the production or purchase inputs are substantiated by special VAT invoices or complete factory costing records, and the export proceeds are collected and repatriated through an authorised bank and reported into the SAFE trade-in-goods foreign-exchange monitoring system. Qualifying offshore digital services are zero-rated only where supplied to a non-resident and consumed outside China; the present goods business follows the physical-export zero-rating route.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Goods Customs Declaration) bearing the export registration number assigned by the General Administration of Customs
Original Bill of Lading, air waybill, or combined transport document evidencing despatch of the goods to a foreign destination
Bank-confirmed Export Proceeds Collection Receipt (foreign-exchange repatriation verification / inward remittance proof for export settlement)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating and any resulting VAT refund are subject to retrospective verification by the STA using customs, banking, and foreign-exchange data. If the goods are not actually exported, the foreign currency is not repatriated within 180 days, or the supporting documentation is false, the STA will reverse the 0% rate, claw back all VAT refunds or credits paid plus late-payment interest, and impose a penalty of 50% up to 500% of the evaded tax under the PRC Tax Administration Law. Fraudulent claims involving forged customs declarations or sham export documents may additionally be prosecuted as export-tax-refund fraud under Article 204 of the Criminal Law, and the partnership and responsible partners may be placed on the serious-tax-offence blacklist.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The People's Bank of China (PBOC) together with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, which has delegated authority over goods-trade verification, capital account registration, and cross-border settlement supervision for all mainland-domiciled foreign-invested partnerships; the Hong Kong SAR is a separate no-exchange-control jurisdiction, but it is not the governing FX regulator for the mainland-registered FIP.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is fully convertible on the current account for bona fide trade, cross-border e-commerce, and service receipts, while the capital account remains controlled. The FIP must repatriate every export and crowdfunding receipt to a domestic bank, retain it in a foreign-currency current account or convert it at a designated bank, and map each receipt to a customs-clearable transaction in the SAFE monitoring system. Crowdfunding advances from Kickstarter and PayPal settlements are treated as advance payments for goods or cross-border trade proceeds only if the FIP can prove shipment of the RPG dice and the absence of third-party collection. Capital contributions from foreign partners require SAFE foreign investment registration, a capital project foreign currency account, a Chinese CPA capital verification report, and post-establishment changes filing; such funds cannot be deployed for prohibited purposes such as unapproved securities investment or entrusted lending. Dividend or profit remittances to non-resident partners are permissible after annual audit, tax settlement under applicable non-resident partnership taxation rules, partnership distribution resolution, and SAFE registration, but banks will reject any distribution if the underlying capital has not been verified or if the exported goods receipts have not been reconciled. The practical hurdle is documentary granularity rather than outright prohibition.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Goods-trade export proceeds must be repatriated to a domestic foreign-currency current account within 90 calendar days of the customs export date unless an SAFE-approved deferred collection registration extends the term. The mandatory conversion ratio is 0%; the FIP may retain 100% of eligible export proceeds in foreign currency or sell them to the designated bank at market rates. Each credit must be matched to the SAFE cross-border receipts-and-payments data, the customs declaration, the commercial invoice, and the logistics proof, and any platform-aggregated advance receipt above the SAFE threshold must be registered before settlement to avoid an automatic trade fraud flag.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI accounts such as Wise, Revolut Business, Payoneer, and Airwallex are not viable as primary banking rails for a mainland-registered FIP. They are not licensed banking institutions in the PRC, cannot receive SAFE registration, cannot support capital verification, and cannot administer RMB basic accounts. PayPal and Stripe likewise act as payment aggregators, not bank alternatives. The FIP must maintain a domestic corporate account with a Designated Foreign Exchange Bank; proceeds from PayPal, Stripe, and Kickstarter should be settled through licensed cross-border payment institutions into that domestic account. Offshore EMI accounts may be used only for paying non-resident suppliers or overseas marketing costs after a lawful outbound remittance has been completed, and such accounts must not be presented as the FIP's primary financial-statement bank in China. Viability rating is low for primary compliance and medium only for narrow ancillary foreign-currency work streams.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The FIP has no statutory director; the general partner or managing partner and all authorized signatories must comply with PBOC face-to-face customer identification requirements. In practice, the responsible person must appear physically at the bank branch in mainland China. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted by major banks for a new FIP entity because the bank must verify original seals, operating licenses, and signatures. If the general partner is a foreign entity or non-resident, a notarized and legalized power of attorney can be submitted, but the appointed local agent must still attend in person with a valid identity document and the corporate seal. Some banks may allow foreign beneficial owners to complete a video interview after the in-person interview of the general partner has occurred, but this remains bank discretion and is not a statutory right.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership chain involving non-resident limited partners in the FIP, particularly where the general partner is a shell entity or where foreign partners hold 25% or more through Hong Kong special purpose vehicles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original and legalized FIP partnership agreement and registration dossier; SAFE foreign investment report; a complete PBOC-compliant beneficial ownership schedule identifying every natural person with 25% or more ownership or control; passport copies and residency proof; source-of-wealth evidence such as bank statements, sale contracts, or tax returns; home-country bank reference letters; and any SPV partner's charter with a chain-of-title notarization.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unsubstantiated crowdfunding inflows from Kickstarter classified as high-volume micro-deposits or anonymous digital backers, creating a mismatch between the FIP's declared low-risk manufacturing scope and aggregate receipts that lack invoiceable trade documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kickstarter campaign contract and platform verification; anonymized backer list; platform payout reports; per-order campaign pledge records; manufacturing timeline; refund policy; customs export declarations for the dice shipments; courier and tracking manifests; a legal opinion concluding that campaign pledges are advance purchases of tabletop products and not securities; and a reconciliation schedule linking every inbound campaign deposit to a distinct fulfilled order.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PayPal and Stripe aggregated settlement flows where the remitting counterparty is the processor rather than the end customer, exposing the FIP to false positives on sanctions screening, anti-money-laundering stage-money suspicion, and possible evasion of foreign exchange reporting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PayPal Business account verification and merchant identity proof; monthly payout CSV or API logs; Stripe settlement reports; a transaction-level reconciliation ledger; e-invoices and customs IDs matched to buyer orders; evidence of sanctions and PEP screening on major backers and counterparties; a written undertaking to maintain a nested order ledger; and a letter from the payment processor confirming that no prohibited person controls the aggregated payout.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Materials and safety inconsistency for epoxy resin and liquid-core dice: the product is described as a simple handicraft, but imports and transport of uncured resin ingredients can raise chemical, customs, and shipping red flags requiring bank investigation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Material Safety Data Sheets for all resins, hardeners, pigments, and liquid-core compounds; supplier invoices and transport packing lists; customs HS classification and duty calculation; product-safety laboratory reports or REACH and Prop 65 compliance certificates for export markets; a chemical storage and waste-disposal plan; and any necessary hazardous-cargo documentation proving lawful custody and transport of all raw materials.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign partners must first complete the SAFE foreign investment information registration for the partnership at the designated bank and obtain the relevant business registration code before any inbound remittance. The remittance should be a SWIFT MT103 from each partner's own overseas account to the FIP's corresponding foreign-currency capital account, with the beneficiary account name identical to the FIP registration name and the remittance purpose code describing a partnership capital contribution by a foreign investor. The bank will verify the transaction against the SAFE system, require the capital contribution declaration, and after receipt the FIP must engage a PRC certified public accountant to issue a capital verification report. If non-resident partners contribute goods, technology, or services instead of cash, separate asset valuation and SAFE registration are required. Converted RMB from the capital account is subject to the negative-list regime: no unapproved securities investment, no entrusted loans, no real-estate purchases outside the business scope, and no non-business investment; all converted RMB must be debited from the RMB capital account to the FIP's ordinary operating account for permitted expenditure.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For raw materials, packaging, and logistics paid to overseas suppliers, the FIP should use SWIFT MT103 with a goods-trade purpose code and the underlying invoice and packing list entered into the bank's electronic trade system. For high-value or repeat resin and dice-mold supplier contracts, a Commercial Letter of Credit issued through SWIFT MT700 is prudent to protect the FIP's deposit; for moderate-value shipments, Documentary Collections through SWIFT MT400 and MT202 provide a lower-cost middle path. For payments to Hong Kong suppliers that accept CNY, use cross-border RMB clearing via the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System, which eliminates FX mismatch and is counted as trade settlement for SAFE reporting. All outbound payments must be matched against verified imports or services; PayPal and Stripe payouts should not be used for supplier settlement because they do not generate SAFE-compliant goods-trade evidence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore forward contracts with a genuine trade background, tenor aligned to invoice maturity, usually not exceeding 12 months without SAFE approval, and limited by bank credit lines.
Plain vanilla FX options or option combinations with forward contracts, used for risk reduction only; exotic, barrier, or leveraged options are prohibited for non-bank corporate clients.

Cross-currency swaps for foreign-currency debt or trade-related principal and interest commitments, with registered foreign debt quota and SAFE approval where applicable; no speculative swap without an underlying exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards are not permissible onshore for the mainland FIP; only offshore CNH NDFs may be used by a separate Hong Kong affiliate for genuine offshore cash-flow exposure, and SAFE will expect no onshore FIP participation in speculative RMB positions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of a Hong Kong Limited Partnership (Form LP2) under the Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 37); Companies Registry filing fee HK$105 assessed at approximately US$13 for the standard FIP with no overdue return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registry, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 calendar days after each anniversary of the date of registration of the limited partnership at the Companies Registry; the anniversary date is the effective registration date of the FIP LP
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing renders the partnership and every general partner in default liable to a Level 3 fine of up to HK$10,000 (approximately US$1,282) plus a daily default fine for continued non-compliance. Persistent failure to file across two consecutive annual cycles, accompanied by an expired Business Registration Certificate and no evidence of active trade, is an administrative forfeiture trigger allowing the Registrar to remove the FIP from the Limited Partnerships Register. The most severe corporate consequence is that limited partners lose the statutory limited-liability shield for obligations incurred while the registration is lapsed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate Renewal under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310); one-year certificate fee comprises Business Registration Fee HK$2,000 plus Protection of Wages on Insolvency Fund Levy HK$150, being HK$2,150 in aggregate, approximately US$276
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal must be completed by the expiry date printed on the current Business Registration Certificate; a statutory grace period of one calendar month after expiry is available before enforcement begins, but interest and penalties are not waived during the grace window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to renew within one month after expiry makes the partnership and every responsible partner liable to a fine of HK$5,000 (approximately US$641) and imprisonment for up to one year, with additional daily default fines. The Inland Revenue Department may cancel the business record, demand immediate payment of all unpaid fees and penalties, and treat the partnership as unauthorised to carry on business. Continued unauthorised trading after cancellation is the primary administrative trigger for deregistration of the FIP business file.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return - Partnership (Form BIS52) under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month from the date of issue of the return. For the standard annual issue on the first business day of April, the base statutory due date is the first business day of May of the same assessment year; a tax representative may obtain the published extension for small partnerships, ordinarily to 15 May for an ordinary workload case
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file without reasonable excuse carries a maximum penalty of HK$10,000 (approximately US$1,282) and, upon prosecution, the court may impose a daily default fine and an additional penalty of three times the tax undercharged. Late or unpaid profits tax bears interest at the quarterly Inland Revenue Department prescribed rate, generally in the range of 7 to 9 percent per year; a 5 percent surcharge applies if tax is unpaid after the original due date and a further 10 percent surcharge after six months. Persistent default permits the Inland Revenue Department to issue a best-of-judgement assessment and to institute criminal recovery proceedings, which will also block renewal of the Business Registration Certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return (Form BIR56A together with Form IR56B for each employee or a nil return) under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month after the date of issue; the annual Employer's Return is normally issued in April each year, and a nil return is required if the FIP has no employees but has received a return from the Inland Revenue Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to furnish the Employer's Return may on conviction attract a Level 3 fine of up to HK$10,000 (approximately US$1,282) together with a daily default penalty; if the omission is attributable to wilful intent to evade tax, the maximum fine is HK$50,000 (approximately US$6,410) and imprisonment may be imposed. Although late Employer's Returns do not directly cause administrative strike-off, a wilful default will be recorded against the partnership and can trigger refusal to renew the Business Registration Certificate.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No automatic statutory audit is imposed on a Hong Kong limited partnership by the Companies Ordinance because the FIP is an unincorporated partnership. The mandatory independent certified CPA audit is triggered by the Inland Revenue Ordinance and Inland Revenue Department administrative practice when the partnership's annual gross turnover for the basis period exceeds HK$5,000,000 (approximately US$641,000). In that case, the Profits Tax Return - Partnership must be accompanied by audited financial statements prepared by a Hong Kong certified public accountant in accordance with Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards. There is no separate balance-sheet or headcount trigger for an unincorporated partnership; however, if the Inland Revenue Department issues a section 51C notice or if any partner is a corporate entity and the Department demands audited accounts, audited financial statements may be required irrespective of turnover. Where annual turnover is HK$5,000,000 or below, the FIP may ordinarily file unaudited accounts and a tax computation unless a specific audit notice is served.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), which are fully aligned with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); a qualifying private entity may elect to apply HKFRS for Private Entities as issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants when preparing financial statements for tax submission. All accounting records must be sufficient to enable the profits or losses of the partnership to be readily ascertained by the Inland Revenue Department.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not impose a separate annual UBO declaration for a Foreign-Invested Partnership. The statutory annual confirmation is made through Form LP2 delivered to the Companies Registry, which must list every general and limited partner, including full name, address, capital contribution, profit share and any changes since the last return. Admission, retirement, assignment of a partnership interest, change in capital contribution or change in profit-sharing ratio must be reported to the Companies Registry within one calendar month of the event. Because the FIP is a partnership, the private-company 30-day shareholding transfer notification window does not apply; the one-month partner-change notice and the annual LP2 return together form the statutory UBO confirmation protocol. Internally, the FIP must maintain a current beneficial ownership and partner register at the principal place of business in Hong Kong for inspection by the Companies Registry, the Inland Revenue Department and other competent authorities, and must continue to satisfy the pass-through and non-resident ownership disclosures required under the Foreign Investment Law framework.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (the partnership equivalent of the Register of Members), showing each general and limited partner's name, address, capital contribution, percentage interest, date of admission and date of cessation

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The Chinese Foreign-Invested Partnership is tax-transparent under PRC partnership tax rules. Resident corporate partners and non-resident partners with a China permanent establishment bear enterprise income tax at 25%. Qualifying incentives include the 15% preferential rate for new/high-tech enterprises, the small low-profit enterprise reduced rate of 20% with an effective 5% rate on taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million during the 2023-2027 period, a 100% super deduction for qualifying R&D expenditure, and an extended 10-year loss carryforward for qualifying high-tech enterprises. The general statutory loss carryforward limit is 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return Form A100000 and supporting schedules, including A105000, A106000, A107010 and A107040, filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration's e-Tax/Golden Tax Phase IV portal; quarterly prepayment returns use Form A200000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly or monthly prepayment returns are also required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual EIT return is due within 5 months after the close of the fiscal year; for calendar-year taxpayers the deadline is 31 May. Quarterly/monthly prepayment returns are due within 15 days after each period. Non-resident partners without a PE and subject only to withholding do not file Form A100000; the FIP as withholding agent must remit withheld tax within 7 days of payment or deemed distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification, entity form and fiscal year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the FIP's Chinese unified social credit code and select Foreign-Invested Partnership. The fiscal year must match the commercial registration and all cross-border withholding filings; mismatched identification codes trigger automatic e-filing rejection and late-filing penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting basis, valuation method and reporting currency
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report on an accrual basis in RMB. If the HK partner's contributions are in foreign currency, translate at the annual average central parity rate. Record all intercompany balances with HK affiliates separately to enable transfer pricing reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating revenue from tabletop RPG dice manufacturing and related e-commerce sales
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal gross receipts attributable to China operations. Sales booked through a HK affiliate must reflect risks, functions and assets; artificial diversion of revenue to the HK entity will be reversed in audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating costs, including epoxy resin, sharp-edge molds, packaging and manufacturing labor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support all costs with Chinese VAT invoices, customs declarations and bank records. Cross-border purchases from HK related parties must be priced under the arm's length standard; intangible-embedded costs for molds or resin formulas require separate royalty WHT and transfer pricing analysis.

Line 5 equals Box 3 minus Box 4. If the FIP's gross margin falls below comparable RPG accessories manufacturers without valid comparability evidence, the tax bureau may apply CUP or TNMM and impose an upward transfer pricing adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment increases and decreases; non-deductible expenditures
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter Schedule A105000 adjustments including disallowed entertainment expenses, thin-capitalization interest, transfer pricing adjustments and tax-exempt income. For pass-through purposes, allocate each partner's distributive share of adjusted taxable income; a HK partner without economic substance cannot unilaterally exclude its share from China's taxing jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-exempt income, deductible losses and credit adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only a substantive treaty-resident partner may claim reduced withholding or credit benefits. Tax-exempt or preferentially taxed income must be proven by a valid Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate and a beneficial-owner statement. Partnership losses are tracked at partner level and may be carried forward by corporate partners subject to continuity-of-interest rules.

The non-resident corporate partner's taxable share is determined by the partnership deed and actual economic contributions. Any change in the profit-sharing ratio shortly before repatriation may be recharacterized as profit shifting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed tax at applicable enterprise income tax rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Resident corporate partners apply 25% or their preferential rate to their taxable shares. A non-resident partner whose partnership activity creates a China permanent establishment files this line at 25%. A non-resident partner without a PE is instead subject to final withholding and is not entered on this line.

A HK resident partner may credit China enterprise income tax against Hong Kong profits tax under the China-HK DTA if treaty benefits are properly approved. Conversely, Hong Kong tax may be creditable against China EIT only for Chinese tax residents. Retain all tax payment vouchers and treaty documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a fine of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 under the Tax Collection Law Article 62, plus daily late-payment interest of 0.05% on unpaid tax. False filing or concealment causing underpayment attracts a 50% to 100% penalty under Article 63; failure to withhold attracts a 50% to 300% penalty under Article 69. Criminal tax evasion arises when unpaid tax exceeds RMB 50,000 and exceeds 10% of tax payable, carrying imprisonment up to 3 years; where the amount is huge and exceeds 30% of tax payable, imprisonment is 3 to 7 years plus fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends or distributions recharacterized as dividends from a Chinese entity to a non-resident corporate investor. Because the FIP is tax-transparent, ordinary partnership allocations from active business profits are taxable at the partner level on a net basis, with no second-level dividend WHT if properly declared; non-compliant distributions disguised as loans or royalties will be recharacterized and subjected to the 10% statutory rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim China-HK DTA relief, the Hong Kong resident corporate partner must: (i) obtain a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate for the relevant year from the Inland Revenue Department; (ii) complete the Chinese tax authorities' Beneficial Owner self-assessment under Announcement 2018 No. 9; (iii) prove substantive business in Hong Kong through office lease, employee payroll, board minutes, strategic decision-making and risk-bearing; (iv) file non-resident contract registration and withholding returns in the Chinese e-Tax system before payment; and (v) preserve all contracts, bank records and tax payment vouchers for at least 10 years. Relief is denied if the HK entity is a bare conduit without core income-generating activities in Hong Kong.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT is 10% for both interest and royalties. Under the China-HK DTA, interest is reduced to 7% and royalties are reduced to 7% for a beneficial owner resident in Hong Kong. Royalty WHT applies to license fees for molds, artwork, product designs and epoxy resin formulas. Interest WHT exemption or reduction is not automatic; the lender must bear real commercial risk, and the borrower must remain within applicable debt-to-equity thin capitalization limits.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and related-party disclosure are mandatory when annual related-party tangible-asset transactions exceed RMB 200,000,000, or when annual intangible-asset transfers, financial-asset transfers or service transactions exceed RMB 100,000,000 each. Master File preparation applies when the ultimate parent group's consolidated annual revenue equals or exceeds RMB 5,000,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China's EIT Law Article 47 and SAT Announcements 2016 No. 42 and
